svg.title: Fixed-step clock: ticks, interpolation fraction and rendered path
svg.desc: FixedStep with step 0.05 s. Top: the returned fraction against time with frames at 10 and 60 per second. Bottom: the damped oscillator rendered at 10 and 60 frames per second lies on one curve, while naive per-frame stepping gives a different path at each frame rate.
svg.text: dashed: ticks every 0.05 s green dots: frames at 60 per second orange rings: frames at 10 per second
α = (T − T₀)/h − K (K = ticks so far); drawn state R(T) = S[K−1] + α (S[K] − S[K−1]) = P(T − T₀ − h)
rendered with FixedStep(0.05): the 60-per-second line, with the 10-per-second frames (rings) on it
naive: one Euler step per frame, 60 per second (dt = 1/60)
naive: one Euler step per frame, 10 per second (dt = 0.1): a different path
x'' = −40 x − 0.8 v, semi-implicit Euler (v += a h; x += v h), x(0) = 1: the oscillator of fixed_steps_follow_the_same_path_at_ten_and_sixty_frames_per_second.
The fixed-step curve is one polyline, delayed by exactly one step (50 ms), whatever the frame rate; naive stepping drifts differently at each rate.
